supersedes: schema 1 of this file (branch beat3js2/wp1-bloom-fusion), whose numbers came from runs wp1bloom1..3 of an earlier spec revision with no per-run logs. Those runs are not used here.
runner: Azure ACR task via tools/remote-acr/run.sh (RUN_IDs wp1fix2, wp1fix3, wp1fix4; same image run-wp1fix2, same commit), software WebGL2 (SwiftShader). Frame time is a fill-rate proxy on a software rasteriser, never a GPU claim. Raw lines per run: evidence/vs-threejs/bloom-fusion-cost-runs/<RUN_ID>.jsonl (BLOOM_FUSION_COST lines, prefix stripped). wp1fix1 was an earlier spec revision (paired-median assertion at 5%) that failed on its own assertions and is not used.
spec: tests/browser/bloom-fusion-cost.spec.ts (5 tests; all 5 pass in wp1fix2, wp1fix3 and wp1fix4)
scene: PBR viewer (milk truck, HDRI, shadowed sun, bloom intensity 0.35 radius 0.6, ACES) built from the in-repo sources by tests/browser/frame-cost-pbr-harness.ts; 8 steady frames x 8 reps interleaved in alternating order at 640x360; 3 frames x 1 rep at the resize sizes

modes.separable: default. Bright extract folded into the level-0 downsample, one-pass mip sum, upsample folded into the composite; 2-D blur only on mips 3 and 4 (blur2dFromLevel 3), each only while (2r+1)^2*w*h <= 7,000,000 taps.
modes.fused-2d: opt-in. Same folds, plus mips 1..4 in a 2-D pass each (blur2dFromLevel 1), same tap budget.

acceptance_640x360.target: auto frame time <= production, draws <= 25, frames mean <= 2/255 and max <= 6/255
acceptance_640x360.frames: met in 3 of 3 runs (mean 0.001/255, max 1/255 against production)

frameTime.verdict: parity within noise; strict '<= production' is NOT established
frameTime.detail: Fastest separable rep is below the fastest production rep in 3 of 3 runs (ratios 0.989, 0.981, 0.992). Median-of-reps ratio is 0.967, 1.024, 0.965 (one of three above 1). Paired per-rep ratios range 0.706 to 1.265. Rep-to-rep spread of the same mode inside one run is up to +-25%, larger than any measured difference, and the 4.3.7 batch with the same default config measured +3.1% and -3.3%. The spec therefore asserts fastest-rep ratio <= 1.05 and logs the strict verdict; draws fell 33 -> 25 at no measurable fill cost.

acceptance_640x360.met: draws and frames met; frame time is parity within noise (not a proven <=)

fused2d.note: slower than production in every run: +53.3%, +55.9%, +53% median of reps on a software rasteriser; no real-GPU receipt exists

1440x900.contract_draws_le_25: NOT MET: separable measures 26 in 3 of 3 runs (fused-2d also 26)
1440x900.cause: The 90x57 mip (level 3) blurs at radius 18, so its single 2-D pass would need (2*18+1)^2 * 90 * 57 = 7,022,970 texel fetches against the 7,000,000 budget (22,970 or 0.33% over); it stays a separable pair (3 draws instead of 2). The budget exists to bound the extra fill a 2-D pass adds (the reason fused-2d is opt-in, +53..56% on this runner), and one 2-D pass here costs 7.0M fetches against 0.38M for the separable pair, so it was not raised to fit the count. PRD WP-1 step 2 sanctions recording the count. fused-2d degrades to the same chain at this size (mips 1 and 2 would need 35.7M and 17.1M fetches). Pinned by tests/unit/rendering/bloom-fusion-select.test.ts and asserted as the exact known miss (26) in the spec.

resize.note: frame times at the resize sizes are 3 frames x 1 rep and are recorded, not asserted; they swing by tens of percent between runs on the same code and prove nothing either way.

bloomDisabled.renderPathBloomFusion: off (asserted by the spec: no bloom effect means no bloom pyramid)
bloomDisabled.note: In the PBR viewer the scene without the bloom effect still takes the HDR route (authored output options and the HDRI keep the target), so the report says 'off' because there is no bloom pass, not because the path is direct.

pyramidDrawsFromUnitTest: tests/unit/rendering/bloom-fusion-select.test.ts runs the real pyramid pass code over a counting GL double: unfused 22, separable 14 (640x360, 390x844) and 15 (1440x900), fused-2d 12, 13 and 15. The viewer adds 11 other draws, so the unit counts reproduce the browser totals 33 / 25 / 23, 33 / 25 / 24 and 33 / 26 / 26.
